title: Paleolithic Neanderthals Used Natural Aspirin
fact: Analysis of 50,000-year-old Neanderthal dental plaque revealed they self-medicated for pain using poplar bark, which contains the active ingredient in aspirin. They also ingested Penicillium mold, showing an awareness of natural antibiotics. Paleolithic hominids understood herbal medicine tens of thousands of years before modern science.

title: Stopping Cyclones With Hair Oil
fact: In 1896, famous scientist Jagadish Chandra Bose wrote the pioneering science fiction story নিরুদ্দেশের কাহিনী (Niruddesher Kahini, "Story of the Untraced"). In the tale, a character calms a massive cyclone by pouring a bottle of কুন্তলীন (Kuntaline, "hair oil") into the ocean. It surprisingly won a literary prize funded by the hair oil's creator.

title: The Empire That Stopped Alexander
fact: In 326 BCE, Alexander the Great halted his conquest of India because his weary troops feared the massive war-elephant army of গঙ্গাঋদ্ধি (Gangariddhi, "wealth of the Ganges"), an ancient empire centered in Bengal. Greek historians recorded that Bengal's ruler commanded thousands of battle-trained elephants, scaring the legendary army into turning back.

title: Speakers With An Internal Compass
fact: The Australian language Guugu Yimithirr completely lacks relative spatial terms like left or right. Instead, speakers use absolute cardinal directions for everything, saying things like there is an ant on your southwest leg. Consequently, native speakers possess a constant, flawless internal compass, even in pitch-black, unfamiliar caves.
